nodes.description: Private uint16 constant-like state variable used as the threshold for the 'Free Will' outcome and in the modulo denominator.
Private uint16 state variable used in the modulo denominator (FREE_WILL + FATE) for random generation.
Private state variable holding the untrusted external contract IReflectionsDataChannel at a fixed address; its methods are invoked for outbound messages.
Public address state variable set from msg.sender in the constructor and used as the sole access-control authority.
Constructor that assigns owner = msg.sender, granting deployer privileges.

Owner-only function computing pseudo-randomness from block data and msg.sender, then making two external calls on the channel contract (postMessage and updateOwner), which is state-changing after external interaction.
Backup owner-only function that calls the external channel.updateOwner(owner), performing an external call without any state update or reentrancy guard.
Caller-controlled address used for owner assignment, access-control checks (require msg.sender == owner) and mixed into the randomness preimage.
Miner/validator-influenceable timestamp included in the keccak256 randomness preimage, making the outcome predictable/manipulable.
Local uint256 result of keccak256(...) % (FREE_WILL + FATE) used to branch between 'Free Will' and 'Fate'.
External call to an untrusted contract (channel.postMessage) executed before the function completes, with no reentrancy protection or effects-first ordering.
External call to an untrusted contract (channel.updateOwner) performed at the end of decide() and inside restoreOwner(), enabling reentrancy into owner-gated functions.

Weak randomness / arithmetic operation: keccak256 over blockhash, coinbase, difficulty, timestamp and msg.sender, then modulo (FREE_WILL + FATE); both predictable entropy and unchecked assumptions on the uint16 sum.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns owner from msg.sender, letting the caller become the access-control authority.
Constructor writes the owner state variable.
msg.sender is encoded into the keccak256 preimage that produces the local random value.
block.timestamp is part of the random preimage, so the outcome depends on miner-influenceable block data.
FREE_WILL is used in the (FREE_WILL + FATE) denominator and in the comparison for the result branch.
FATE is used in the (FREE_WILL + FATE) denominator of the modulo operation.
Result of the randomness/arithmetic computation is stored in the local variable random.
decide() computes and controls the local random variable used for branching.
FREE_WILL is read in the 'random < FREE_WILL' branch condition.
decide() invokes the untrusted external contract via channel.postMessage without a reentrancy guard.
decide() invokes the untrusted external contract via channel.updateOwner as the last statement.
decide() reads owner in 'require(msg.sender == owner)' to gate privileged execution.
Caller-controlled msg.sender determines whether decide() proceeds past the owner check.
Caller-controlled msg.sender determines whether restoreOwner() proceeds past the owner check.
restoreOwner() reads owner to validate the caller's authorization.
restoreOwner() performs an external call to the untrusted channel contract with no guard.
The untrusted channel contract could re-enter decide() during channel.postMessage before execution completes.
The untrusted channel contract could re-enter decide() during channel.updateOwner.
The untrusted channel contract could re-enter restoreOwner() during channel.updateOwner.

normalization_plan.reason: The local variable random exists only inside decide() and should be collapsed into that function node, keeping the dataflow from block.timestamp/msg.sender and the unsafe randomness operation attached to the function.
